reason: The control objective requires testing and approval of changes to AI systems. Article 9 (Risk Management) mandates a lifecycle approach, which includes change management. Article 15 (Data and Data Governance) requires data quality and integrity, which are impacted by changes. Article 17 (Record-keeping) supports documentation of changes. Article 72 (Obligations of Distributors) ensures that changes are managed throughout the supply chain. Together, these provisions provide a defensible and sufficiently complete regulatory basis for the control objective.
applicability_note: This control is applicable to all AI systems under the EU AI Act, as changes to any component (model, prompt, knowledge base, plugin, security) can affect the system's risk profile and compliance with the Act.
challenge_comment: The challenge is to ensure that all types of changes are consistently tested and approved, not just code changes. The mapping must cover changes to data, models, and other components that can impact the system's safety and compliance.
